sections.h2: What is the quickest way to move a house in Hackensack?
sections.html:
Start with the fewest open items: a passed fire inspection, a clear tax balance and a price grounded in recent Hackensack sales. Hackensack is the Bergen County seat and the county's largest municipality, with 46,030 residents in 2020 and an estimated 46,380 by July 1, 2025.

Only 36.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so renting dominates the housing stock. An owner of a two-family house or a small building should expect tenants, leases and rent questions to come up during the sale. Agents, private sales and cash buyers all follow the same city inspection, tax payoff and recording steps. A cash buyer simply removes the lender's appraisal and approval from the timeline.

The city sits about 12 miles northwest of Midtown Manhattan on 4.35 square miles, and each block can differ from the next. The west side has single-family homes, some on lots of an acre or more. Older central blocks have two-family houses, Prospect Avenue and the garden complexes offer apartment living at scale, and downtown has mixed-use buildings.

sections.h2: Figures that should shape your asking price
sections.html:
Hackensack pairs a renter-heavy population with a large tax bill: the average home was billed $10,307 in 2025.

The 2025 general tax rate is 3.209 per $100 and the effective rate is 2.527. Average sale prices ran about $75,000 above the average assessment, so base your number on nearby closed sales and not on the tax card.

sections.h2: Fire inspection before a Hackensack sale
sections.html:
The Fire Prevention Bureau issues a Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance, and a seller needs it before closing. The city's form lists a $70 fee, a six-month validity period and issuance on the day of the inspection.

If the house fails or nobody is home for the appointment, the city charges a new fee on a new application. The form asks for the buyer's name, the seller's name and the real estate company, and wrong details void the report.

The requirement comes from the state Uniform Fire Code, which calls for a smoke alarm certificate whenever a one-family or two-family dwelling is sold, leased or changes occupants. Only the municipality can issue it. Prepare the house first:

  • Smoke alarms on every level including the basement, in shared stairwells and hallways, and within 10 feet of each sleeping area.
  • Sealed ten-year battery alarms in place of old ones, since the state Division of Fire Safety advises swapping alarms every decade.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm and a portable fire extinguisher, both listed on the city form.

Also ask the Building, Housing and Land Use department whether other resale paperwork applies to your type of property.

Taxes fall due on the first day of February, May, August and November, and each date carries a 10-day grace period. Late balances up to $1,500 accrue 8 percent annually, and anything above that accrues 18 percent. Everything must be paid by November 10 to avoid the accelerated tax sale starting November 11.

New owners should know that the county can take three to six months to record a deed and tell the city, so a buyer should send the collector a mailing address after closing. Request a written balance from the collector before you review the closing statement.

Owners who think the assessment overshoots market value can appeal to the Bergen County Board of Taxation at Two Bergen County Plaza in Hackensack. The annual filing date is April 1. Property assessed above $750,000 may go straight to the Tax Court by April 1.

The state charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded, set by the rate table for the sale price. A graduated percent fee applies above $1,000,000, and the Division of Taxation lists that schedule.

  • The state transfer fee, collected at recording.
  • The $70 fire certificate.
  • Mortgage payoff and any recorded liens.
  • The seller's portion of the quarter's property tax.

Resident sellers sign the GIT/REP-3 residency certification so the clerk will take the deed. Out-of-state sellers prepay Gross Income Tax, with a floor of 2 percent of the sale price unless a listed assurance covers them. An executor's deed to an heir named in the will falls under the state's list of exempt transfers. A sale to an outside buyer is taxed, and the fire certificate is still required.

sections.h2: How should a landlord handle a Hackensack rental sale?
sections.html:
Roughly 63 percent of occupied homes here are rented, and typical rent is $1,911. The Department of Building, Housing and Land Use also staffs the Rent Stabilization Board, so check with that office on whether your building is covered before you price from market rents.

The state fire certificate applies to leases as well as sales, so a tenant turnover and a sale may each need an inspection. Book the inspection late enough that the six-month certificate still covers your closing date. Have an attorney read every lease, because the buyer steps into the occupancy.

sections.h2: Roads and rail lines buyers use
sections.html: Interstate 80, Route 17, Route 4 and County Route 503 cross the city, and bridges at Court Street, Midtown and Anderson Street span the Hackensack River. The Pascack Valley Line stops at Anderson Street and Essex Street on its way to Hoboken and connections to Penn Station New York. Buses leave the Hackensack Bus Terminal for the Port Authority and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station. A listing close to a station or the terminal puts that commute in front of buyers.

sections.h2: Order of steps for a quick sale
sections.html: Book the fire inspection first, then ask the tax collector for a written balance. Pull your deed, the latest tax bill and any lease or payoff statement for your attorney. If the house came through an estate, the estate signs a GIT/REP form for its residency status. Once the certificate is in hand, a cash buyer can move to closing on the date you both set, with the attorney recording the deed and the state filings.

faqs.q: Is a fire inspection certificate mandatory for a Hackensack sale?
faqs.a: Yes. State rules require a smoke alarm certificate for one-family and two-family sales, and the city fire bureau issues it for $70 on a form that also covers carbon monoxide alarms and a portable fire extinguisher. It stays valid for six months.

faqs.q: Who pays the state transfer fee on a Hackensack sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it at recording, and it scales with the sale price under the state's schedule. Exemptions are limited to the transfers the state lists, such as a deed between parent and child.

faqs.q: Does a Hackensack house with unpaid taxes still sell?
faqs.a: It can, once the balance is cleared at or before closing. The city wants current-year taxes paid by November 10 to avoid the tax sale that begins November 11, and late balances accrue interest at 8 percent up to $1,500 and 18 percent above.

faqs.q: May I sell while tenants live in the house?
faqs.a: Yes, a tenant-occupied house can sell. Ask the Building, Housing and Land Use department about rent stabilization and have an attorney read every lease.

faqs.q: What changes when the house came through an estate?
faqs.a: The estate signs a GIT/REP form for its residency status, and an executor's deed to an heir named in the will is exempt from the transfer fee. A sale to an outside buyer is taxed, and the fire certificate is still required.
